jobs.description: SummaryImagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas quickly become extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences. Bring passion and dedication to your job, and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Smart people and inspiring, innovative technologies are the norm here.Our team is responsible for validating the RF performance of top-notch, monolithic, cellular transceivers and the RF subsystems built around them. In order to expand our team's validation capability towards future Apple products, we are looking for a passionate RF engineer with strong RF transceiver system understanding, complemented by AI/ML and programming skills. jobs.occupation: Doctoral Researcher (f_m_x) - Forest Carbon Attribution from Earth Observation and Atmospheric Const (Geowissenschaftler/in)
jobs.description: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: “Taking the pulse of the Earth to safeguard a habitable planet.”For section 1.4 Remote Sensing and Geoinformatics (https://www.gfz.de/en/section/remote-sensing-and-geoinformatics/overview) (department “Geodesy” (https://www.gfz.de/en/departments/geodesy) ), we are looking for a:Doctoral Researcher (f_m_x) - Forest Carbon Attribution from Earth Observation and Atmospheric ConstraintsReference Number 11590Many countries rely on forests to meet their climate targets, but how much of the forest carbon sink is real, and how much depends on management and disturbance, remains largely unverified. This PhD will combine satellite observations, carbon-cycle models, and atmospheric measurements to build an independent picture of forests’ actual role in the climate.This position is part of EUFOR-G3W, a Horizon Europe project contributing to the WMO Global Greenhouse Gas Watch (G3W). EUFOR-G3W develops observation- and model-based products to quantify greenhouse-gas sources and sinks at global to national scales.Within the EUFOR-G3W project, GFZ contributes to the development and application of harmonised Earth Observation (EO) datasets to improve our understanding of forest carbon dynamics. The research focuses on forest biomass, age, disturbance history, and vegetation productivity, as well as their integration into the FLUXCOM-X empirical flux upscaling framework to better represent managed and recovering forests.The successful candidate will investigate how forest management, disturbances, and recovery processes influence the land CO₂ budget across different spatial and temporal scales. A particular focus will be on combining satellite-based observations with carbon flux estimates and assessing how atmospheric observations can independently constrain these contributions.The candidate will be supervised by GFZ and Wageningen University and Research (WUR), (https://www.wur.nl/en) in collaboration with Max Planck Institut for Biogeochemistry (MPI-BGC) Jena (https://www.bgc-jena.mpg.de/en) . They will work closely with a second PhD candidate in the group of Wouter Peters at WUR, Netherlands. Together, the two positions form a duo linking observations and models: the GFZ position focuses on translating Earth Observation data into forest carbon information, while the WUR position focuses on forest and atmospheric modelling and data assimilation. Your research will have direct relevance to international climate policy: Your results will feed into operational greenhouse-gas monitoring systems supporting the WMO Global Greenhouse Gas Watch and the Copernicus CO2 monitoring service. You will have access to a unique combination of global forest EO datasets, cloud-native analysis infrastructure, forest ecosystem models, and atmospheric inversion systems. And you will be in close collaboration with leading European groups at WUR and MPI-BGC Jena within the EUFOR-G3W consortium.Your responsibilities:- Translate high-resolution EO forest datasets (e.g. biomass, forest age, disturbance) into model-ready inputs for forest and atmospheric models, while preserving key spatial information- Quantify the contribution of forest management and disturbance to forest CO2 exchange using model simulations constrained by EO data- Assess how well atmospheric CO2 observations can independently constrain this signal across regions and timescales- Contribute to improving the representation of managed and recovering forests in data-driven flux products such as FLUXCOM-X- Derive national forest carbon budgets and compare them with greenhouse-gas inventory reporting- Publish results in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences and project meetingsAbout You:Essential Qualifications:- An MSc in Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Physical Geography, Atmospheric Sciences, Remote Sensing, or a related quantitative field- Strong quantitative and data analysis skills- Proficiency in Python and experience with geospatial or large environmental datasets- Good written and spoken English- Ability to work in a collaborative, multi-institutional research environmentDesirable Qualifications:- Experience in terrestrial carbon cycle science, ecosystem modelling, or Earth Observation of forests- Familiarity with atmospheric inverse modelling or greenhouse-gas accounting frameworks- Experience with Xarray, Dask, or cloud-based geospatial data analysis- Knowledge of national greenhouse-gas inventories or LULUCF accountingWe do not expect applicants to be already experts across all three disciplines — Earth Observation, forest modelling, and atmospheric inversions. The position is specifically designed to bridge them.Start date: 1st February 2027Fixed-term: 36 Monate (extension to 4 years possible, subject to funding)Salary: Die Stelle ist nach TVöD Bund mit der Entgeltgruppe 13 bewertet. jobs.description: What to ExpectWe are the engineers powering the world's largest fast-charging network, Tesla's Supercharger fleet. jobs.occupation: 3 Research Assistants (PhD Positions) (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Europa-Universität Viadrina is an internationally and interdisciplinarily oriented university located in the twin city of Frankfurt (Oder)-Słubice, on the German and Polish banks of the River Oder, where it educates around 4,000 students from all over the world. The university lives the European idea in its everyday practice and promotes European integration through teaching and research. With around 300 academic and 300 nonacademic staff, it forms a community for which successful communication and cooperation with Eastern Europe are a particular concern.The Entrepreneurship Research Lab (ERLab) (https://entrepreneurshipresearchlab.com/)  at the Faculty of Business Administration and Economics invites applications for 3 Research Assistants (PhD Positions)in the field of Entrepreneurship Research on Ecosystems, with a focus on Creativity, Communication, and CommunityJob ID 1216-26-01Working time: 30h/weekSalary: as per tariff (group 13 TV-L (https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/c/t/rechner/tv-l/allg?id=tv-l&g=E_13&s=1&zv=VBL-Ost&z=75&zulage&stj=2026&stkl=1&lst4f&r=0&zkf=1&pvk=0&kk=15.5%25) , 75 %) Duration: 4 years, fixed termStarting Date: 01.01.2027The "Entrepreneurship Research Lab: Research on Creativity, Communication, and Community (ERLab)" project at the European University Viadrina Frankfurt (Oder) conducts research on entrepreneurial ecosystems in a research-practice partnership with Campus Founders gGmbH in Heilbronn.The primary place of work is the university campus in Frankfurt (Oder). Extended research stays in Heilbronn and at other entrepreneurial ecosystems in Europe are an integral part of the position; flexible working arrangements are possible within the university’s regulations.Your responsibilities include:- conducting research on regional entrepreneurial ecosystems, focusing on one of the ERLab’s three research areas: creativity, communication, or community- developing and completing an empirical PhD dissertation project in the respective research area- contributing to the ERLab’s research activities and publications in scientific journals- presenting research findings at international meetings and conferences- organizing knowledge transfer events in Heilbronn- contributing to a knowledge database on entrepreneurship research- participating in other scientific activities of the ERLabThe ideal candidate is expected:- to have an MSc degree (or equivalent) in business, management, or related areas; - to have a pronounced interest in research on entrepreneurship and ecosystems with a focus on one of the scholarly fields of creativity, communication, or community;- to have substantial and applied knowledge of qualitative research methods, such as case studies, that are typically used in entrepreneurship, management, and organization research; - to be familiar with entrepreneurial ecosystems, especially in Germany and Eastern Europe;- to have strong communication skills and the ability to learn quickly;- to be fluent in English (written and spoken, at least C1 CEFR) and to have at least B1-level proficiency in German.We offer:- attractive remuneration with financial stability, regular pay adjustments, and an annual special payment- occupational benefits (e.g. retirement provision through VBL, capital-forming benefits, job ticket)- collectively agreed annual leave plus non-working days on 24 and 31 December- flexible working arrangements and family-friendly working conditions- and much more… (https://www.europa-uni.de/de/universitaet/arbeitgeberin/stellenangebote/index.html)Your applicationWe look forward to receiving your application no later than 17.11.2026. Interested applicants should send their application as one PDF file (prefer­ably as one doc­u­ment) with the Job ID mentioned above to: bewerbung@europa-uni.de (https://mailto:bewerbung@europa-uni.de) . Please indicate in your application which of the three research areas (creativity, communication, or community) you would like to focus on. The file will be deleted immediately after the selection process. For further information about the position, please contact Univ.-Prof. Dr. Jochen Koch (koch@europa-uni.de).Applications should include a letter of motivation, a curriculum vitae (CV), and degree certificates and transcripts.The Europa-Universität Viadrina Foundation is actively committed to diversity and equal opportunity among all its staff and pursues the goal of being a non-discriminatory institution that welcomes and protects people in their diversity within the university community.Further information can be found at: www.europa-uni.de/stellenangebote (http://www.europa-uni.de/stellenangebote)
